correctness.rationale: Explicit de Bruijn edge construction gives one mandatory copy of each binom(k,2) target edge and a k-1 edge one-marker cycle; all graph degrees balance and every target rotation orbit meets the added cycle. For necessity, subtracting mandatory edges from a closed walk gives an integral circulation. A hypothetical <k-1 edge augmentation splits into short periodic walks; Fine–Wilf shows distinct primitive-support walks cannot meet, while a short periodic walk meeting the adjacent-ones target orbit meets no other target orbit. The mandatory graph has at least two disjoint orbits for k>=4, contradicting connectedness. Constructive and exhaustive small-case checks succeeded.

value.rationale: The family of all binary weight-two k-mers is a canonical fixed-composition target in universal cycles and sequence assembly. The formula gives the exact shortest possible cyclic host for every k>=4 and a constructive optimum, quantifying the unavoidable price of connecting isolated necklace cycles rather than a routine example or isolated numerical improvement.
